title: Cut three bites off a sausage with a knife and fork: tines pin the round, slick link while the knife saws through
instruction: Cut three bite-size pieces, 1.5 to 2.5 cm long, off the sausage with the knife and fork, keeping everything on the plate, then lay the knife and fork down.
context: Cutting food on a plate with a knife and fork is something nearly everyone does at most meals. A cooked sausage is round (3 cm across) and slick on a glazed plate: pressed and dragged by a knife alone it rolls or skids, so the fork's tines go in through the skin (about 2.5 N, estimate) and hold the link while the knife saws through to the plate, within a few cm of the fork; tilt or pull the fork and its tines tear out. Unlike food steadied by hand on a board, the only hold here is the fork's tines through the food's top, worked against the knife in the other hand.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y toward the left arm, heights above the table top. (1) A white glazed dinner plate, 26 cm across (Corelle Winter Frost White 10-1/4 in dinner plate or similar), its flat floor 19 cm across and 1.3 cm above the table, its rim rising 1.6 cm to its edge, centred at (30, 0) on a 32 x 32 cm, 3 mm black non-slip mat (Dycem or similar) that keeps it from moving. (2) On it, one fully cooked smoked bratwurst link (Johnsonville Smoked Bratwurst, 5 links per 14 oz pack, about 80 g), 3.0 cm across (2.8 to 3.2 cm), trimmed to 13 cm, lying left to right across the plate's middle, centred at (30, 0); from the fridge or at room temperature, never heated; a fresh link every trial. (3) A stainless dinner fork, 19 cm, four tines 3.5 cm long curving 20 degrees down from the handle (Oneida Chef's Table dinner fork or similar), lying face up left of the plate along y, tine tips at (30, 15) on the table pointing at the plate, its handle on a 5 x 1.6 x 1.15 cm wooden block at y 31.5. (4) A stainless serrated table knife, 24 cm (Oneida Chef's Table B327KDTF 9-1/2 in dinner knife, sold with a serrated edge and round tip: blade 10.5 x 2 cm, handle 13.5 cm), standing edge down in a slotted wooden rest right of the plate, along x, blade toward +x, the blade's heel at (24.5, -20.5); the rest is an 11 x 5 x 0.4 cm base with two 11 x 0.8 x 2.4 cm walls leaving a 4 mm slot, centred at (30.7, -20.5). Nothing else is on the table. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged over the whole trial and at its end. 0 if a gripper ever touches the sausage (video; simulation: PhysX contact between any robot link and the food) or any of the food leaves the plate (any piece's middle more than 12 cm from the plate's centre, or below its floor). A piece counts when it is cut fully off (after the trial it lifts away on the fork alone, nothing joining it to the rest), is 1.5 to 2.5 cm long (ruler) and lies on the plate, and the fork's tines were in the sausage while the cut that freed it was made (video). 0.25 per counted piece, at most 0.75. 1.0: three counted pieces, the knife and the fork both let go and lying on the plate (each one's middle over the plate, no part more than 5 cm above the plate's floor, the fork not stuck in the food), both grippers open and at least 3 cm from them, everything still for 1 s. A utensil left on the table, held, or stuck upright in the food: at most 0.75. Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: A fresh link every trial (sausage is consumed); wipe the plate and wash the fork and knife between trials; grease touches only the utensils and the plate, never the grippers.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (Isaac Sim, PhysX, 20 Hz). The link is 13 rigid 1 cm slabs glued end to end; a finished cut frees a joint and parts the faces a few mm. Rules (estimates): tines go in at 2.5 N within 55 deg of the skin's normal, hold until pulled 3 N or levered 35 deg; a held knife cuts 0.3 mm per mm sawn while pressing 1 N or more, or presses through at 8 N; skin resists 600 N/m; strokes drag it at most 1.2 N; through at 4 mm from the plate. Utensils pass through the food; plate fixed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps). The left arm (left of the video) rose and drifted back toward its base; the right arm closed its gripper and from about 60 s hovered 4-5 cm above the table beside the knife's handle. Neither touched the fork, the knife or the sausage. Demo: 1.0.
